newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Mediocredito to bid for Banco di Napoli.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Mediocredito to bid for Banco di Napoli.

text.p: Italian state-owned credit institute Mediocredito Centrale said on Thursday it had decided to make an offer for 60 percent of ailing southern bank Banco di Napoli.
Mediocredito said in a statement the board had mandated chairman Gianfranco Imperatori and managing director Giorgio Tellini to arrange the offer.
Earlier, Italy's Banca Nazionale del Lavoro (BNL) said it had decided with insurer INA to submit a bid.
The Italian Treasury set Friday, December 20 as the deadline for bids.
It took temporary control of Banco di Napoli, Italy's largest southern bank, after it unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995.
The bank plunged a further 674 billion into the red in the first half of this year and the Treasury has given interested parties until December 20 to make offers.
The Treasury said on Tuesday it had kicked off a 1.977 trillion lire capital increase for the ailing bank, beginning the underwriting for the operation. $1=1,530
